title: fleet-inventory-matching-policy-and-transport-friction-analysis
content:
Overview:
This working sheet captures a different lens on GPU fleet procurement: matching inventory (by family/series) to regional demand while explicitly modeling transport friction (transit variability, customs hold, cross-dock delays). The goal is a simple operational ordering policy that reduces stockout probability for latency-sensitive tenants while avoiding heavy overcommitment in regions with slow transit lanes.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: infra procurement, capacity planning, SRE on-call, and finance for commit sizing.
- Scope: Global fleet (NA / EU / APAC) across three accelerator families (A100-class, H100-class, and low-cost Q8 quantized variants). Focus is on 12-week runway and reorder cadence planning.

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Demand baseline: steady-state token throughput growth = +5% w/w for latency-sensitive routes (internal forecast).
- Allocation cushion: 12% net cushion for Hosted API bursts; 20% for Dedicated enterprise pools.
- Transit lead-time mean and jitter derived from last 18 months manifest data; customs and port strikes modeled as heavy-tail events with 1 in 40 probability (adds +14 days).
- Transfer lanes availability (inter-region transfers) assumed limited to 10% of fleet at any time without advance manifest.

Data snapshot (as-of 2025-01-10):
| Region | Preferred family | On-hand units | Committed reqs (4w) | Allocated runway (weeks) | Transit mean (days) | Transit jitter (sd days) | Reorder trigger (units) | On-order ETA window | Notes |
|-------:|------------------:|--------------:|--------------------:|------------------------:|-------------------:|------------------------:|-----------------------:|---------------------:|------|
| NA     | H100-class        | 720           | 420                 | 10                      | 14                 | 6                       | 240                   | 2025-02-08 -> 2025-02-20 | strong enterprise demand, low customs risk |
| EU     | A100-class        | 480           | 360                 | 8                       | 18                 | 9                       | 200                   | 2025-02-14 -> 2025-03-02 | port congestion in Rotterdam window |
| APAC   | Q8-variants       | 260           | 200                 | 6                       | 22                 | 12                      | 120                   | 2025-02-20 -> 2025-03-08 | higher lead-time variance, air freight option expensive |

Interpretation notes on table:
- Allocated runway weeks = (on-hand - committed) / (avg weekly burn for region).
- Reorder trigger includes 2-week safety buffer + 1.5*lead-time-sd to account for jitter clustering.

Lead-time jitter model (simple):
- We model ETA as Normal(mu=mean_transit, sigma=transit_jitter) with a heavy-tail event: with probability p_strike = 0.025 (approx historical 1 in 40), add a blockout delay sampled Uniform(10,18) days.
- Effective buffer days = ceil(mu + 1.65*sigma + p_strike*14) -> used to set reorder lead-time allowance.

Order phasing recommendation (12-week horizon):
1) Staggered manifest lanes: prefer 3-phase arrival windows for NA/H100 orders to spread customs and DC intake load. Example: orders of 500 H100 -> split into 200/150/150 spaced by 10 days.
2) Mixed transport strategies: for APAC Q8 shortfalls, prefer partial air lift (10–15% of units) for critical enterprise bursts rather than full sea manifests; reserve air lanes as an emergency option in contracts.
3) Pre-approved cross-dock transfers: establish a 30-unit daily transfer SLA between EU and NA hubs for short-term rebalancing (requires customs pre-clear).

Cost vs risk trade-offs (qualitative):
- Option A: Bulk sea orders (lower capex/unit) but higher jitter -> reduces per-unit cost by ~12% vs small frequent orders. Increases stockout tail risk.
- Option B: Hybrid sea+air for critical SKUs -> +9–14% per-unit cost but improves worst-case availability for top 10% of latency-sensitive traffic.

Operational rules (policy bullets):
- Soft reorder trigger: when on-hand <= reorder_trigger (table) signal procurement to start manifest negotiation.
- Hard reorder commit: if forecasted runway <= 4 weeks for any region + family, auto-approve emergency allocation up to 15% of committed spend for cross-region transfers or expedited freight.
- Allocation tagging: label arriving manifests by family+region+batch_id, enable immediate assignment to canary capacity pools for smoke-tests before full rollout.

Simulations run (summary):
- Monte Carlo 1,000 runs using daily burn & lead-time jitter: baseline policy (single bulk reorder per 8 weeks) resulted in 9% stockout probability for APAC within 12 weeks.
- Staggered manifesto policy reduced stockout probability to 3.1% at the cost of ~3% higher logistics overhead.
- Hybrid air reserve (15% of manifest) reduced tail risk to 1.2% at +11% unit logistics cost.

Open risks and unknowns:
- Port strike correlation: current heavy-tail parameter is based on 2023–2024 episodes; correlation across regions during geopolitical events could be higher.
- Transfer friction legal: cross-border temporary transfers may require additional import/export filings that could add unpredictable delays. Need legal signoff.
- Model sensitivity to demand shock: a single enterprise customer onboarding high-throughput routes can double regional burn inside 4 weeks — require canary quota limits.

Action items (owners & dates):
- Aisha: finalize manifesto split templates for H100 orders (deliver 2025-01-20).
- Marcus: draft expedited air-lane SOW with two freight partners and cost bands (deliver 2025-01-27).
- Lena: run sensitivity runs for 5 enterprise-onboarding shock scenarios and publish results (deliver 2025-01-24).
- Ravi: legal review on cross-dock temporary transfer process (deliver 2025-01-30).

Appendix (quick formulas):
- Reorder trigger units = ceil(weekly_burn*effective_buffer_weeks) + cushion_units
- effective_buffer_weeks = (mu_days + 1.65*sigma_days + p_strike*14) / 7
- cushion_units = max( round(0.12 * forecasted_weekly_burn*4), 20 ) // ensures minimum cushion

Notes to reviewers (bullet):
- This is a working sheet: numbers are illustrative — procurement should validate vendor lead-times and freight timetables before commit.
- Prefer feedback on the strike probability parameter and acceptable unit-cost increase for hybrid air lanes.

Quick links and references:
- Historical manifests dataset: JIRA-INF-4521 (see attachment)
- Freight partners RFP: CONF-Infra-Transport-Notes-3287
- Ops PR for transfer workflows: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/912

Bottom line recommendation (short):
Adopt a staggered manifest policy for primary families and hold a small, contracted air-reserve for APAC and enterprise-critical bursts. Formalize cross-dock transfer pre-clear to enable 10% short-term rebalancing. These actions reduce tail stockout risk materially at modest incremental logistics cost.
